newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Central African leader clamps curfew on capital.
newsitem.headline: Central African leader clamps curfew on capital.

text.p: Central African Republic President Ange-Felix Patasse has clamped a night curfew on the capital Bangui where a two-week-old army mutiny has triggered an exodus of terrified residents.

In a radio and television address on Saturday night, Patasse hinted he would use force to put down the army mutiny, the third this year. French troops based in Bangui under bilateral accords helped quell a more serious uprising in May.

"In my position as commander-in-chief of the armed forces, I could indeed have ordered military operations to bring this rebellion to an end, but it would have brought harm to the civilian population," Patasse said. "Thus I was patient. I issue two demands: lay down your arms - immediately and unconditionally," he told mutineers.
Sporadic gunfire could be heard in Bangui on Sunday following a sustained exchange of heavy fire on Friday night.
Church-mediated talks between the government and soldiers have been blocked by rebel demands for Patasse's resignation, something the president has rejected.
Soldiers have hardened long-running grievances over pay and status into political demands, which have split the army between troops from Patsse's northern region and those from the south.
Southerners are suspected of allegiance to former president Andre Kolingba, one of the candidates defeated by Patasse in multiparty elections in 1993.
